Taking the triangular-lattice primitive translations as \((1,0)\) and \((1/2,\sqrt3/2)\), the \(\sqrt3\times\sqrt3\) supercell is rotated by \(30^\circ\). Its reciprocal translations may be written as \((4\pi/3,0)\) and \((-2\pi/3,2\pi/\sqrt3)\).

The reduced hexagon has circumradius \(4\pi/(3\sqrt3)\). Its corners occur at
\[
\left(\pm\frac{2\pi}{3},\pm\frac{2\pi}{3\sqrt3}\right),
\qquad
\left(0,\pm\frac{4\pi}{3\sqrt3}\right),
\]
with alternating corners belonging to \(K\) and \(K'\). Thus, counterclockwise,

\[
\boxed{K\ (2.09,1.21)\;;\ K'\ (0,2.42)\;;\ K\ (-2.09,1.21)\;;\ K'\ (-2.09,-1.21)\;;\ K\ (0,-2.42)\;;\ K'\ (2.09,-1.21)}
\]

The original hexagonal Brillouin zone has circumradius \(4\pi/3\). A \(\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}\) periodicity reduces every reciprocal-space dimension by \(1/\sqrt{3}\), so the reduced-zone circumradius is \(4\pi/(3\sqrt{3})\). Thus its corners occur at angles \(0^\circ,60^\circ,\ldots,300^\circ\):

\[
\boxed{\left(2.42,\,0.00\right);\ \left(1.21,\,2.09\right);\ \left(-1.21,\,2.09\right);\ \left(-2.42,\,0.00\right);\ \left(-1.21,\,-2.09\right);\ \left(1.21,\,-2.09\right)}
\]

A commensurate \(\sqrt3\times\sqrt3\) supercell rotates the reduced hexagonal zone by \(30^\circ\) and reduces its corner radius from \(4\pi/3\) to \(4\pi/(3\sqrt3)\). Thus the vertex components are \(2\pi/3\approx2.09\), \(2\pi/(3\sqrt3)\approx1.21\), and \(4\pi/(3\sqrt3)\approx2.42\).

\[
\boxed{(2.09,\,1.21);\ (0.00,\,2.42);\ (-2.09,\,1.21);\ (-2.09,\,-1.21);\ (0.00,\,-2.42);\ (2.09,\,-1.21)}
\]

The transverse hopping \(2t\) leaves only one band active at \(n=7/8\). Away from half-filling, \(U=8t\) opens neither a charge gap nor a spin gap in this effective one-dimensional band. The resulting state has gapless charge and spin excitations, identifying it as a Luttinger liquid rather than a spin-gapped Luther–Emery liquid.

\[
\boxed{\text{(a) Luttinger liquid}}
\]

The transverse hopping \(2t\) splits the ladder into bonding and antibonding bands. At \(n=7/8\), only one band remains active at low energy. Away from half filling, the repulsive interaction \(U=8t\) leaves both spin and charge modes gapless, giving an ordinary Luttinger liquid rather than a spin-gapped Luther–Emery liquid.

\[
\boxed{a}
\]

Scaling dimensions are extracted after tensor-network coarse-graining reaches a fixed point: inspect the singular values, coarse-grain to convergence, construct the transfer matrix, and analyze its eigenvalues.

\[
\boxed{a;b;c;d;i}
\]

For \(J>0,J>J'>0\), the ground state is uniformly magnetized. Although two spin-rotation generators are broken, they form one conjugate pair, producing one quadratic Goldstone mode.

For \(J<0,J<J'<0\), frustration produces a coplanar spiral with zero total magnetization. The spiral completely breaks \(O(3)\), so its three broken generators yield three independent Goldstone modes.

\[
\boxed{n_{FM}=1\;;\;n_{AF}=3}
\]

\[
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
J>0,\ J>J'>0:\quad O(3)\rightarrow O(2).
\text{ The two broken spin rotations form one conjugate pair, giving one quadratic Goldstone mode.}\\
J<0,\ J<J'<0:\quad
\text{the noncollinear spiral completely breaks }O(3).
\text{ With no ferromagnetic moment, all three broken rotations give independent modes.}\\[2pt]
n_{FM}=1\;;\;n_{AF}=3
\end{gathered}}
\]
